name: JennyStudio GEO Factory
author: Brain1981@JennyStudio

sections.description:
JennyStudio GEO Factory is a Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) toolkit. It keeps your content assets organized and turns them into native WordPress posts with the help of AI models that you connect yourself.

AI connections on Settings -> Connectors

  • DeepSeek (models: deepseek-flash, deepseek-v4-pro)
  • Qwen via Alibaba Cloud Bailian pay-as-you-go OpenAI-compatible endpoint (/compatible-mode/v1, models: qwen3.8-max, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.8-flash)
  • GLM via Zhipu AI BigModel OpenAI-compatible endpoint (/api/paas/v4, models: glm-5.3, glm-4.7, glm-5.3-flash)
  • Kimi via Moonshot AI OpenAI-compatible endpoint (/v1, models: kimi-k2.6)
  • Hunyuan via Tencent Cloud TokenHub OpenAI-compatible endpoint (/v1, models: hy4-preview, hy3)
  • Volcengine Ark pay-as-you-go endpoint (/api/v3, chat models: Doubao-Seed-2.1-pro and Doubao-Seed-2.1-lite)
  • Volcengine Ark Coding Plan endpoint (/api/coding/v3), with the same chat models plus the fixed embedding model doubao-embedding-vision
  • API keys are verified with one authenticated request only when you save the Connectors settings; simply viewing the screen never triggers a remote request

Content assets

  • Title libraries and keyword libraries in dedicated custom database tables; every title keeps a usage count, and duplicate entries are removed automatically when bulk-adding
  • A prompt library with copy, edit and delete management, plus variable hints ({{title}}, {{keyword}}, {{knowledge}})
  • A knowledge base using a dedicated internal content type with a bundled Markdown editor
  • Knowledge-base chunking into a dedicated chunks table using a rule-based or an AI-assisted semantic strategy; the table already reserves vector columns for future embedding support
  • One unified AI provider and model picker on the plugin settings screen; the model is chosen from a dropdown of available models instead of being typed manually
  • Export selected title libraries, keyword libraries, prompts and knowledge bases as a single JSON file, and import such a file to move data between sites; imported names receive a date-time suffix

Article generation

  • Generates native WordPress posts (the built-in post type) with native categories and tags
  • Choose one title from a library or enter your own, select up to five keywords, up to five knowledge bases, and the prompt template; the configured AI model is displayed on the screen and cannot be set inconsistently across screens
  • Generate excerpts and FAQ entries for existing posts directly in the editor; FAQ entries are stored as structured pairs and reused for FAQPage schema output
  • Generated posts are listed under JennyStudio GEO Factory -> Article Management and are marked in the native Posts list through a dedicated AI column

Structured data and llms.txt

  • Outputs a JSON-LD schema graph (Organization/Person site entity, WebSite, BlogPosting/WebPage, BreadcrumbList and FAQPage built from generated FAQ entries); when Yoast SEO is active it only supplements Yoast’s graph with the FAQPage piece, and it stands down entirely while Rank Math is active
  • Serves a dynamic /llms.txt following the llmstxt.org convention, refreshed automatically when content changes; the generator yields to Yoast SEO and Rank Math to avoid conflicts

External Services

This plugin requires connecting at least one of the third-party AI services described above. Every request is sent directly from your WordPress site to the chosen provider over HTTPS, using the API key you configured on the native WordPress Settings -> Connectors screen. The plugin author never receives your content, requests or API keys.

Third-Party Components

The plugin bundles the following GPL-compatible third-party components, with their full license texts included alongside the corresponding files:

  • EasyMDE 2.18.0 (MIT License), which bundles CodeMirror (MIT License) — Markdown editor
  • Font Awesome 4.7.0 (MIT License for CSS, SIL Open Font License 1.1 for the web font) — editor icons
  • Parsedown 1.8.0 (MIT License) — Markdown to HTML conversion; loaded under a plugin-specific class name to avoid conflicts with other plugins
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it through the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate JennyStudio GEO Factory through the Plugins screen.
  3. Open Settings -> Connectors and connect at least one AI provider.
  4. Open the JennyStudio GEO Factory menu in the admin sidebar, pick the AI model in the plugin settings, manage assets and generate articles.
sections.changelog:
1.5

  • Add AI model connections: Qwen (Alibaba Cloud Bailian), GLM (Zhipu AI BigModel), Kimi (Moonshot AI) and Hunyuan (Tencent Cloud TokenHub).
  • Add a quick model availability test tool on the plugin settings screen.

1.4

  • Add WordPress Multisite compatibility.

1.3

  • New JSON-LD structured data (Schema) engine: outputs a complete schema graph (Organization/Person site entity, WebSite, BlogPosting/WebPage, BreadcrumbList, and FAQPage built from generated FAQ entries) when no SEO plugin is active; when Yoast SEO is active it only supplements Yoast’s graph with the FAQPage piece instead of duplicating it, and it stands down entirely while Rank Math is active. New settings control the feature and the site representation (organization name and logo, or a represented person whose profile data is used), reading Yoast SEO’s own settings as fallback.
  • New llms.txt generator: serves /llms.txt dynamically following the llmstxt.org convention, with the site name and tagline, per-post-type link lists of the latest content with excerpt-based descriptions, top taxonomy term sections, and a sitemap index link. The file refreshes automatically when content changes, and the generator yields to Yoast SEO’s llms.txt feature and to Rank Math to avoid conflicts. A settings toggle with a direct view link controls the feature.

1.2

  • New setting to choose the content post types (post, page and custom post types) used for material sourcing and article generation; WordPress reserved types, editor-less types and well-known non-content types from plugins such as ACF, Elementor, WooCommerce and popular form/slider plugins are excluded, and the exclusion list can be extended via the geo_factory_excluded_post_types filter.
  • The source-article picker in the Knowledge Base editor shows post IDs next to titles, supports searching by title or post ID, and offers post type checkboxes (at least one must stay selected) to filter keyword search results; direct ID lookup still finds a post regardless of type.
  • Generated articles can now be saved as any enabled post type via a new Post Type radio option on the generation form; categories and tags are only assigned when the chosen type supports them.
  • The generated-articles list now covers all enabled post types, shows a Post Type column, and lists articles in every language when WPML is active; the AI marker column also appears on the native list tables of all enabled post types.
  • Knowledge Base editor safeguards: the chunk button is disabled with a notice until a new document is saved, saving requires a non-empty title and content, and clicking the chunk button with unsaved changes now saves the document first and then runs chunking automatically.
  • Prompt Library moved above Knowledge Base in the menu, “Knowledge Document” wording unified to “Knowledge Base” (English and Chinese), and the Publish button on Knowledge Base edit screens is relabeled as Save.

1.1

  • Fix known bugs.
  • Improve the article generation interaction experience.

1.0

  • Initial release.

  • Title and keyword libraries with bulk import

  • Prompt template library
  • AI knowledge base with rule-based and semantic chunking
  • DeepSeek and Volcengine Ark (pay-as-you-go and Coding Plan) connections on the native Connectors screen
  • Native WordPress article generation with publishing options and an AI marker in the Posts list
  • JSON export and import of title libraries, keyword libraries, prompts and knowledge documents
